examples.en: The ball got caught in the net.
I hit the ball over the net.
A volleyball net is higher than you think.
The net is low, so the ball goes over easily.
In table tennis, the ball must go over the net.
The players set up the net before the match.

explain: 테니스, 배구, 탁구처럼 공을 넘기는 운동에 쓰는 말이에요. 물고기를 잡는 것은 '그물'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used in sports where the ball goes over a divider, such as tennis, volleyball, and table tennis. The net for catching fish is called 'geumul'.

examples.en: The child played happily, popping soap bubbles.
When the wind blew, the soap bubbles floated up into the sky.
We played with soap bubbles in the park.
Soap bubbles pop right away when you touch them.
A lot of soap bubbles form when I wash the dishes.
I bought my little sibling a bubble toy.

explain: '비눗방울을 불다', '비눗방울을 날리다', '비눗방울이 터지다'처럼 함께 쓰는 동사를 같이 외워 두세요. '거품'은 여러 개가 뭉친 덩어리를 말할 때도 쓰지만, '비눗방울'은 동그랗게 하나씩 뜬 방울이에요.
explain_en: Learn it with its verbs: '비눗방울을 불다' (blow), '날리다' (float up) and '터지다' (pop). '거품' (foam) can be a whole mass of bubbles, while '비눗방울' is a single round bubble floating on its own.

examples.en: The concert tickets have already been booked.
Train tickets can be booked from a month ahead.
A text arrives once the ticket is booked.

examples.ko: 좌석이 예매되는 데 몇 초밖에 안 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took only a few seconds for the seats to be booked.

examples.ko: 인기 있는 영화는 빨리 예매돼서 표를 구하기 어려워요.
examples.en: Popular movies get booked fast, so tickets are hard to get.
Can a booked ticket be canceled?

explain: 표를 미리 사는 사람은 '예매하다'를 쓰고, 표가 미리 팔린 상태는 '예매되다'로 말해요. '표를 예매했어요'와 '표가 예매됐어요'처럼 주어가 달라요. '매진되다'는 표가 다 팔렸다는 뜻이라 달라요.
explain_en: The person buying a ticket in advance uses '예매하다', and the ticket's state is described with '예매되다': '표를 예매했어요' versus '표가 예매됐어요'. '매진되다' is different; it means the tickets are sold out.

examples.ko: 마라톤 참가자들은 아침 일곱 시까지 출발선에 모여 주세요.
examples.en: Marathon participants, please gather at the starting line by seven in the morning.
I waited for the signal at the starting line.
It is a foul if you cross the starting line.
The children stood side by side in front of the starting line.
My heart pounded when I stood at the starting line.

examples.ko: 모두 출발선 뒤로 한 발 물러나세요.
examples.en: Everyone, please step back behind the starting line.

explain: 반대는 '결승선'이에요. 달리기뿐 아니라 사람이 시작하는 조건을 비유할 때도 써요. '출발선이 다르다'는 처음부터 조건이 불공평하다는 말로 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 집안 형편이 달라서 출발선이 다르다는 말이 나와요.
phrases.en: People say we do not start from the same line because our family situations differ.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람마다 처음 가진 조건이 달라 공정하지 않다는 느낌으로 써요. 사회 문제를 이야기할 때 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say people begin with unequal conditions, implying unfairness. It often comes up when discussing social issues.
phrases.en_equiv: not start on a level playing field

explain_en: The opposite is '결승선' (finish line). Besides races, it is used figuratively for the conditions people start with. '출발선이 다르다' often means the starting conditions are unfair from the beginning.
